rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results <U+2013> two-year field experiment (2012<U+2013>2013) in Inner Mongolia comparing five drip fertigation levels on potato with own measurements of yield, irrigation amounts, SMP, IWP and PFP (Tables 2 and 4, Figs 2<U+2013>5).
rows.notes: The study compares fertilizer rates under drip fertigation; all plots are drip-irrigated, so there is no comparison of drip against another irrigation method and no measurement of evaporation, runoff or water saving. It reports irrigation water productivity per fertigation level (Table 4) and total applied water (92.6<U+2013>173.2 mm), but no own result that drip conserves water or minimizes evaporation/runoff. Statements about sandy soil leaching and water scarcity are from the introduction, citing other work.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results <U+2013> two-year field experiment on sand and loamy sand soils comparing five drip fertigation levels for potato, reporting own data on yield, irrigation water applied, SMP and IWP (Tables 1, 4; Figs 2<U+2013>4).
rows.notes: The experiment is on sandy soil and uses drip fertigation scheduled by soil matric potential at 20 cm, but the experimental factor is fertilizer dose, not irrigation method. No comparison with traditional/other irrigation methods, no measurement of water wastage, runoff or evaporation. The only comparison with LEPA is of enterprise yields (31.5 and 33.0 Mg/ha), not water use. Hence no own evidence that drip reduces water wastage in sandy soils relative to other methods.

notes: Full text appears complete. Primary two-year field trial of drip fertigation levels for potato on sandy soil; the water-conservation claims attributed to it by the review are not tested in the study (no irrigation-method comparison, no evaporation or runoff measurements).
